greet.text: Physician Amsel Fenn. If you've been in the Lanes, wash your hands.

choices.text: It isn't the Passengers. It's the new millstone: its dust is in the Lanes' well.

why.text: Because the fever started there and stays there. Passengers live close and travel far. I'm a physician, not a poet: I follow where the sick are.

choices.text: (Alchemy) The sheen, the metal taste, a fever with no cough: that's residue in the water, not contagion.
Come and look at the well with me. If I'm wrong, I'll say so in the square.

convinced.text: He goes with you, looks a long time, and says nothing on the walk back. In the square that evening he says it loudly: the fever is the water, and the water is the mill's. Some people even listen.

refuses.text: "Bring me something better than a story." (You could still shut the mill's pipe yourself.)
